label: PLA Warns 3 Philippine Aircraft Over Scarborough Shoal — Aug 21, 2026
notes: PLA Southern Theater Command said it tracked, monitored and issued verbal warnings to three small Philippine government aircraft — an Islander, a Cessna C-208, and a PA-31T — that 'illegally intruded' into airspace over Scarborough Shoal (Huangyan Dao) without Chinese government approval, calling the flights a 'serious violation' of sovereignty 'highly likely to cause misunderstanding and miscalculation.' The Philippine embassy in Beijing did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment.
platform: Islander, Cessna C-208, PA-31T (Philippine government aircraft)

label: CCG 4305 — Unauthorized EEZ Patrol Off Zambales — May 19-21, 2026
notes: CCG 4305 detected ~48nm west of Pandaquit, Zambales by Canada's DVS Program. PCG deployed Piper Navajo 302 aircraft and BRP Cape San Agustin to confront vessel. Three-day unauthorized patrol (May 19-21) before withdrawal. First documented CCG unauthorized patrol along Luzon's western coast.

label: PLAN Frigate 532 Dangerous Maneuver vs. BRP Benguet — Mar 25, 2026
notes: PLAN missile frigate 532 made an 'unsafe and unprofessional maneuver' closing in at dangerous distance against BRP Benguet (LS-507) near Pag-asa Island. AFP WESCOM called it 'intentional.' Col. Nep Padua cited COLREGs violations. China counter-claimed (March 28) that BRP Benguet 'ignored radio warnings.' Third PLAN warship incident in the Spratlys in three weeks (after March 7 fire-control radar lock on BRP Miguel Malvar at Sabina Shoal).

label: Resupply Mission — Aug 5, 2023
notes: Unaizah May 1 got through; Unaizah May 2 repelled by CCG water cannons. BRP Malabrigo and BRP Cabra escorted. China deployed ~14 vessels to intercept.

label: Resupply Mission — Dec 10, 2023
notes: 46 Chinese ships vs 4 Philippine vessels. Water cannons disabled one ship's engines. CCG collided with supply ship carrying AFP Chief of Staff. Major escalation; both sides accused the other of ramming.

label: Resupply Mission — Feb 4, 2024
notes: China fired water cannons at BRP Cabra and supply boats. Navigation bridge damaged; crew injuries. China called the Philippine approach 'deliberate provocation.' US condemned the use of water cannons.

label: Unaizah Mae 4 Attack — Mar 23, 2024
notes: CCG water cannon barrages destroyed Unaizah Mae 4 superstructure and disabled propulsion. BRP Sindangan towed stricken vessel back. Four Philippine Navy sailors injured. Philippines filed diplomatic protest.

label: Resupply Mission — Jun 17, 2024 (Most Serious)
notes: China deployed 8 small craft; CCG personnel boarded Philippine RHIBs with bladed weapons. 8 sailors injured (1 lost thumb); M16 rifle, ammo, food and supplies seized. Only second time China succeeded in blocking resupply since 2021. US condemned; MDT invocations followed.
damage: 2 Philippine RHIBs destroyed; M16 + ammo + supplies seized

label: Resupply Mission — Jul 2024 (Provisional Arrangement)
notes: Following June 17 incident, Philippines and China announced provisional resupply arrangement in July 2024. Arrangement broke down within weeks as China resumed water cannon use claiming Philippines attempted to transport construction materials.

label: Resupply Mission — Aug 2024 (Arrangement Collapse)
notes: Multiple water cannon incidents followed collapse of provisional arrangement. Philippine RHIBs damaged. Gen. Brawner confirmed personnel injuries. Both sides blamed each other for violating the July 2024 understanding.

label: Pag-asa Island Supply Route
notes: Supply route from El Nido, Palawan to Pag-asa (Thitu Island), Philippines' largest occupied Spratly feature. Chinese maritime militia vessels maintain persistent presence around Thitu Island, surveilling Philippine supply missions.

label: CCG Patrol: Fiery Cross → Second Thomas Shoal
notes: Routine China Coast Guard patrol route from Fiery Cross Reef command hub to blockade position near Second Thomas Shoal. Average transit ~3 hours at full speed. CCG deployed 14+ vessels per intercept mission by 2023.

label: CCG Patrol: Mischief Reef → Second Thomas
notes: Short patrol route from Mischief Reef (largest Spratly outpost) to Second Thomas Shoal intercept position. Mischief Reef is the closest major Chinese outpost to Second Thomas Shoal. CCG vessels stage from here for immediate intercept operations.

label: CCG Patrol Route: Fiery Cross → Scarborough
notes: China Coast Guard patrol route connecting Fiery Cross Reef command hub to Scarborough Shoal enforcement zone. CCG maintains continuous presence at Scarborough Shoal entry point, blocking Philippine fishermen. Water cannon incidents in December 2023, April 2024, October 2024, December 2024.

label: China Militia: Subi Reef → Pag-asa Harassment
notes: Chinese maritime militia vessels routinely deploy from Subi Reef (16 nm from Pag-asa) to circle and surveil Philippines' largest Spratly outpost. CSIS AMTI documented militia at Pag-asa 'in greater numbers and on a more constant basis than ever before' since 2021.

label: China Militia: Fiery Cross → Whitsun Reef (Mar 2021)
notes: ~220 Chinese maritime militia vessels assembled at Whitsun Reef, first sighted December 2020, reported publicly March 7, 2021. Organized and staged from Fiery Cross, Subi, and Mischief Reefs. By March 31, vessels dispersed to McKennan/Hughes Reefs and near Pag-asa Island.

label: PLA Navy: Hainan → Spratly Islands Patrol
notes: Routine PLAN surface combatant and submarine transit from Yulin Naval Base (Hainan) to Spratly Islands operating area. PLAN increased patrols significantly after 2020. Type 055 destroyers, Type 052D destroyers, and Type 075 LHDs deployed to South Sea Fleet for SCS operations.

label: PLA Paracel Military Exercises — Jul 2020
notes: China conducted military exercises around the Paracel Islands July 1–5, 2020. US called the drills a violation of 2002 Declaration on Conduct. US responded by deploying USS Nimitz and USS Ronald Reagan carrier strike groups for first dual-carrier SCS exercises since 2014.

label: PLA Taiwan Encirclement — Aug 2022 (Post-Pelosi)
notes: Largest PLA exercises since 1996 Third Taiwan Strait Crisis, triggered by Speaker Pelosi's Taiwan visit. Live-fire, ballistic missiles over Taiwan, nominal blockade simulation. ~450 PLA aircraft entered Taiwan ADIZ in August 2022—highest monthly total ever. Before Pelosi: 23 median line crossings total; after: 563 incursions in 2022 alone.

label: 'Joint Sword' Exercises — Apr 8-10, 2023
notes: PLA Eastern Theater Command 'all-round encirclement' after Tsai-McCarthy meeting in California. 232 PLA aircraft near Taiwan in 3 days; 134 entered ADIZ. Su-30s and H-6 bombers. Matched Pelosi-era numbers in less than half the time.

label: 'Joint Sword-2024A' — May 23-24, 2024
notes: Response to President Lai Ching-te's inauguration. 111 aircraft and 46 naval vessels around Taiwan; 82 crossed median line. First time China Coast Guard participated alongside PLA in joint military operations around Taiwan.

label: China Patrol: Fiery Cross → Sabina Shoal 2024
notes: China deployed up to 40 ships (including 3 PLAN warships) to Sabina Shoal during the 2024 standoff with BRP Teresa Magbanua. First time PLAN warships participated alongside CCG in Spratly area confrontation. BRP Teresa Magbanua rammed August 31, 2024.

label: US FONOP: Near Subi Reef
notes: US Freedom of Navigation Operation within 12 nm of Subi Reef, asserting the artificial island has no lawful territorial sea. US has conducted FONOPs in the South China Sea regularly since 2015. China's PLAN typically shadows US vessels during FONOPs and issues warnings.

label: US FONOP: Near Fiery Cross Reef
notes: US FONOP challenging excessive Chinese maritime claim within 12 nm of Fiery Cross Reef. USS Ralph Johnson (DDG-114) conducted FONOP February 2022 near Fiery Cross. China's PLAN issued 15 warnings and deployed aircraft/ships. US NavForces WEST-NAVEUR confirmed 'lawful navigation.'

label: US FONOP: Near Mischief Reef
notes: US Freedom of Navigation Operation within 12 nm of Mischief Reef, the largest Chinese artificial island and the one within Philippines' EEZ. USS Milius (DDG-69) conducted FONOP March 2023. China claimed the vessel 'illegally intruded.' US stated it conducted 'lawful freedom of navigation operations.'

label: US Dual-Carrier Exercise — Jul 4-9, 2020
notes: USS Nimitz (CVN-68) and USS Ronald Reagan (CVN-76) carrier strike groups conducted simultaneous exercises in South China Sea during China's Paracel exercises—first dual-carrier SCS drills since 2014. Explicit response to Chinese military exercises and Pompeo's July 13 rejection of Chinese SCS claims.

label: US Carrier Transit: Luzon Strait → SCS
notes: Routine US Navy carrier strike group transit through the Luzon Strait into the South China Sea. USS Carl Vinson primary SCS carrier 2024–2025. US carriers operate from the South China Sea to demonstrate freedom of navigation and deter Chinese aggression against the Philippines.

label: US P-8A Poseidon Maritime Patrol Route
notes: Routine P-8A Poseidon maritime patrol aircraft route from Andersen AFB Guam through the South China Sea. China has intercepted P-8s multiple times: PLA J-11 released chaff in P-8 flight path (2021); J-16 performed 'unnecessarily aggressive maneuver' causing P-8 to fly through turbulence (2023). US continues patrols regardless.

label: US-Philippines Joint Patrol: Scarborough Area
notes: US-Philippines joint maritime patrols near Scarborough Shoal, resumed under Marcos administration. US Coast Guard vessels joined Philippine Coast Guard patrols. China protested joint patrols as 'provocative.' US cited them as demonstration of treaty alliance obligations.

label: US-Philippines Joint Patrol: Second Thomas
notes: US Navy vessels conducted joint patrols with Philippine Coast Guard near Second Thomas Shoal following escalation of Chinese harassment. Task Force Ayungin (revealed November 2024 by Secretary Austin) is the dedicated US unit supporting Philippine forces at Second Thomas Shoal.

label: NMESIS Anti-Ship Coverage: Luzon Strait
notes: 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment's NMESIS launchers positioned at Batanes Islands during Balikatan 2025 cover the Luzon Strait with ~100 nm Naval Strike Missile range. Any Chinese surface vessel transiting from Pacific to South China Sea through Luzon Strait falls within engagement range. First overseas NMESIS deployment.

label: Balikatan 2024 — First Exercise Outside Territorial Waters
notes: Balikatan 2024 exercise area extended for first time beyond Philippines' 12 nm territorial waters, directly challenging Chinese EEZ claims. France participated as full partner. Live-fire missile test sank target vessel. ~16,000 US, Philippine, Australian, French troops.

label: US FONOP: Near Scarborough Shoal
notes: US vessels transited near Scarborough Shoal during Balikatan 2024 exercises, coinciding with a Chinese water cannon attack on Philippine vessels (April 30, 2024). US State Department condemned China's actions at Scarborough as 'dangerous and provocative.' US Freedom of Navigation asserts Chinese presence does not constitute lawful territorial waters.

label: AUKUS Submarine Transit: Lombok Strait → SCS
notes: Planned transit route for future AUKUS nuclear-powered submarines from HMAS Stirling (Western Australia) through Lombok Strait into South China Sea. Nuclear-powered submarines transit Lombok Strait to avoid shallow Malacca Strait. SRF-West at HMAS Stirling to begin in 2027 with up to 4 US Virginia-class submarines.

label: AUKUS Partner Route: Singapore → SCS
notes: Route for US Littoral Combat Ships rotating from Changi Naval Base, Singapore into South China Sea patrol areas. UK Royal Navy and Australian warships also transit this route. Singapore-based US vessels provide sustained presence monitoring Spratly Islands and EEZ intrusions.

label: Strategic Transit: Malacca Strait → SCS
notes: Main shipping lane through Malacca Strait to South China Sea. 85,000+ vessel transits per year; 30%+ of global trade. China's 'Malacca Dilemma'—dependence on this US Navy-secured route is a strategic vulnerability. A South China Sea conflict could threaten this $5.3T annual trade corridor.

label: Japan-Philippines Joint Maritime Patrol
notes: Following signing of Japan-Philippines Reciprocal Access Agreement (July 8, 2024), Japan MSDF and Philippine Navy conduct joint maritime patrols in the South China Sea. Philippines is the first Asian nation to sign such a pact with Japan. RAA entered into force September 2025.

label: Japan MSDF South China Sea Transit
notes: Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force vessels transit the South China Sea increasingly as Japan deepens Indo-Pacific engagement. Japan has conducted freedom of navigation operations and intelligence-gathering missions. Kishida: 'Ukraine today may be East Asia tomorrow.' Japan hosted first trilateral US-Japan-Philippines summit April 2024.

label: CCG Floating Barrier — Scarborough Shoal 2023
notes: China deployed a floating barrier (water boom) at the southeast entrance to Scarborough Shoal in September 2023. Philippines physically removed it. Another floating barrier deployed December 2023 with simultaneous water cannon attacks on 3 Philippine vessels. China also placed barriers at BRP Sierra Madre approach area October 2023.
damage: Barrier used to block Philippine access to traditional fishing grounds

label: DF-26B/DF-21D Test Fires — Aug 26, 2020
notes: China fired anti-ship ballistic missiles (DF-21D 'carrier killer' and DF-26B 'Guam killer') into the South China Sea on August 26, 2020 during PLA exercises. Trajectory approximately from inland China to South China Sea impact zone. US confirmed the launches. China said they demonstrated ability to strike 'moving targets at sea.'

label: US-Philippines Patrol: Second Thomas Area 2023
notes: US and Philippine vessels conducted joint maritime patrols south of Palawan toward Second Thomas Shoal corridor. Marcos administration reinstated and expanded joint patrols after Duterte era freeze. US Coast Guard and Navy vessels participated alongside Philippine Navy and PCG.

label: PLAN Transit: Hainan → Pacific (Luzon Strait)
notes: Routine PLAN naval transit from Yulin Naval Base (Hainan) through the Luzon Strait into the Philippine Sea / Western Pacific. China has increased frequency of such transits, practicing 'island chain breakout' scenarios. US monitors all PLAN Pacific transits via P-8 and submarine surveillance.

label: France Joins Balikatan 2024 as Full Partner
notes: France participated as a full partner (not observer) in Balikatan 2024 for the first time, marking Europe's direct military engagement in South China Sea defense. French warship transited from Singapore to Philippine waters for the exercise. France's engagement reflects European concern over Indo-Pacific security and free navigation.

label: PLA Combat Readiness Patrol: Hainan → Scarborough — Mar 30, 2026
notes: PLA Southern Theater Command published video of combat readiness patrols near Scarborough Shoal on March 30, featuring two Type 054A guided-missile frigates and J-15 carrier-based fighters. PLA described mission as 'tracking, monitoring, warnings, and expulsions' — a direct response to Philippine 'provocations' following the BRP Benguet near-collision (March 25). Escalatory deployment of carrier-based aviation alongside surface combatants in the South China Sea.

label: CCG Cutters: Scarborough → Batanes Islands (Bashi Channel) — Apr 2026
notes: Three Chinese coast guard cutters (each 330+ ft) tracked 'bracketing' the Philippines' northernmost Batanes Islands near the Bashi Channel — the strategic waterway between Luzon and Taiwan. Described by analyst Ray Powell as 'a new level of aggression.' Batanes is closer to Taiwan than to Manila. Coincides with Balikatan 2026 preparations and NMESIS deployments to Batanes area.

label: Japan JSDF Combat Deployment: Balikatan 2026
notes: Japan will send combat-capable Self-Defense Forces units to Balikatan 2026 (starting ~April 20) for the first time since WWII, with troops carrying weapons during joint exercises. Exercise focuses on coastal defense, anti-ship tactics, and area denial. Australia and France also participating. AFP Chief declared it 'biggest ever' despite US-Iran conflict.

label: CCG Floating Barrier Deployment: Scarborough Shoal — Apr 10-11, 2026
notes: China installed a 352-meter floating barrier at the entrance channel to Scarborough Shoal between April 10-11, 2026, using 4 Chinese fishing vessels and a CCG patrol vessel. Part of a wider pattern of SCS access restriction documented by FDD (April 16, 2026). ~10 CCG vessels maintained above-average presence near Scarborough April 5-12. Third deployment of a floating barrier at Scarborough (after Sept 2023 and Dec 2023 incidents). Philippine officials condemned the barrier but did not announce immediate removal plans.

label: Japan JSDF Naval Transit: Okinawa → Balikatan 2026 Exercise Zone
notes: Japan Self-Defense Forces deploying 1,400 troops plus naval vessels from Okinawa/Kyushu area south to Balikatan 2026 exercise staging areas in northern Luzon (April 20–May 8, 2026). Japan's contribution includes Type 88 Surface-to-Ship Missile systems — the first time Japan has deployed anti-ship missiles capable of denying Chinese naval access to the South China Sea in a formal Philippine exercise. This marks Japan's most direct military engagement in SCS defense exercises since WWII.

label: US-Australia-Philippines Trilateral MCA — Apr 9-12, 2026
notes: Four-day multilateral Maritime Cooperative Activity (MCA) conducted April 9-12 by US, Australian, and Philippine naval forces within the Philippine EEZ. Included warships, fighter jets, and surveillance aircraft. Second such trilateral MCA of 2026; immediately preceded by PLA Southern Theater Command 'tracking and expulsion' statement on April 13 accusing Philippines of 'rallying extra-regional countries.'

label: Japan Type 88 SINKEX — BRP Quezon, Balikatan 2026
notes: Japan Ground Self-Defense Force Type 88 Surface-to-Ship Missile (SSM-1) live-fire exercise against decommissioned Philippine Navy vessel BRP Quezon (PS-70) during Balikatan 2026 (April 20–May 8, 2026). First time Japan has fired anti-ship missiles in a combined exercise in the Philippines since WWII. Trilateral coordination between JSDF, AFP, and US forces. Type 88 has ~150 km range with active radar homing. Japan's Defense Minister Koizumi observed from Manila. Exercise demonstrates US-Japan-Philippines sea-denial capability in the South China Sea approach and Luzon Strait corridor.

label: Liaoning Carrier: Taiwan Strait Transit Southbound — Apr 20, 2026
notes: Chinese aircraft carrier Liaoning (16) transited the Taiwan Strait southbound on April 20, 2026 — the first PLAN carrier transit of the Taiwan Strait since Fujian's December 2025 passage. Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense confirmed and released surveillance imagery. Assessed by The Diplomat as strategic counter-signaling: Liaoning appears to be preparing for joint naval-air exercises in the South China Sea, timed to coincide with Balikatan 2026's opening day. Stars and Stripes (April 21) and Taipei Times confirmed the transit. Combined with the simultaneous 133rd Task Group Western Pacific deployment, analysts assessed China was executing a dual-axis counter-demonstration.

label: PLA 133rd Task Group: Western Pacific → Yonaguni-Iriomote Return — Apr 22, 2026
notes: China's PLA Eastern Theater Command 133rd Naval Task Group (Baotou Type 052D destroyer + Huanggang Type 054A frigate) completed Western Pacific combat readiness training and returned through the Yonaguni-Iriomote Waterway on April 22, 2026. China publicly announced the return transit — an unusual disclosure assessed as deliberate messaging. Free Malaysia Today characterized it as 'tit-for-tat' after Japan's MSDF Ikazuchi transited the Taiwan Strait ahead of Balikatan 2026. Task group had deployed outbound via the Yokoate Channel on April 19. Full Western Pacific circuit (Apr 19-22) forms a symmetrical counter-exercise timed to match every day of Balikatan 2026's opening phase.

label: PLA Zunyi YJ-20 Hypersonic Missile Exercise — East of Luzon, Apr 27, 2026
notes: Type 055 destroyer Zunyi fired YJ-20 hypersonic anti-ship cruise missile (Mach 6+ cruise, Mach 10 terminal, 1,000–1,500 km range) during exercises east of Luzon on April 27, 2026. PLA released footage as a direct counter-signal during Balikatan 2026's second week. Line represents approximate exercise trajectory in the Philippine Sea. From this position, YJ-20 range covers the entire South China Sea, Philippine Sea, and allied naval formations participating in Balikatan 2026. South China Morning Post: 'timed to heat up South China Sea as Balikatan drills continue.'

label: PLA Task Group 107: Live-Fire Drills East of Luzon — Apr 24–25, 2026
notes: China's PLA Southern Theater Command announced Naval Task Group 107 conducted exercises in waters east of Luzon Island, Philippines on April 24–25, 2026. Drills included live-fire shooting, sea-air coordination, rapid maneuvers, and maritime replenishments testing 'integrated joint combat capabilities.' PLA described the operation as 'a necessary action in response to the current regional situation.' Exercise directly flanks Luzon from the east (Philippine Sea side), complementing China's earlier Balikatan 2026 counter-moves: Liaoning carrier Taiwan Strait transit (April 20), 133rd Task Group Western Pacific circuit (April 22), and Type 076 Sichuan SCS sea trials (April 22+). Task Group 107 composition not publicly disclosed. Philippine embassy did not immediately respond. Sources: Xinhua, GMA News, Japan Times.

label: DESRON-7/Task Force Ashland MME: Subic Bay → NOLCOM/Luzon Strait — Apr 28-29, 2026
notes: DESRON-7 and Task Force Ashland conducted Multinational Maritime Events (MME) with Philippine, Canadian (HMCS Charlottetown), and JMSDF ships in the NOLCOM area bordering the Luzon Strait on April 28-29 (Balikatan 2026 Days 9-10). Line from Subic Bay staging area to Luzon Strait MME zone. USNI News (April 28) reported that a Chinese naval action group was simultaneously operating nearby. This is the most concentrated allied naval presence in northern Philippine waters since the Cold War.

label: PLA Naval Action Group: Hainan → Luzon Strait Vicinity — Apr 28, 2026
notes: USNI News reported a Chinese naval action group operating in proximity to US missile deployments near the Taiwan approach and Luzon Strait area on April 28, 2026 (Balikatan 2026 Day 9). Assessed as distinct from PLA Task Group 107 (April 24-25 east-Luzon drills). Deployment point assessed as Luzon Strait vicinity based on USNI reporting and standard PLAN transit routes from Yulin Naval Base. The simultaneous presence of US NMESIS/missiles and this PLA action group creates an active mutual deterrence dynamic at the Luzon Strait chokepoint — the most sensitive waterway for any Taiwan or SCS contingency.

label: PLA STC Combat Readiness Patrols: Fiery Cross → Scarborough Shoal — Apr 30, 2026
notes: PLA Southern Theater Command deployed naval and air forces for combat readiness patrols at Huangyan Dao (Scarborough Shoal) and surrounding territorial sea/airspace on April 30, 2026 (Balikatan 2026 Day 11). Framed as countermeasures to Balikatan 2026. China Coast Guard conducted simultaneous law-enforcement patrols. AFP called it 'information operations.' Line shows patrol route from Fiery Cross Reef command hub. Source: Xinhua (April 30).

label: Balikatan 2026 Day 11: Subic Bay → West PH Sea MME Zone — Apr 30, 2026
notes: 11-ship multinational naval formation (Philippines, US, Japan, Australia) conducted CASEX, GUNNEX, PHOTOEX in the West Philippine Sea on April 30, 2026 (Balikatan Day 11). Ships include BRP Miguel Malvar, BRP Antonio Luna, USS Ashland, JS Ikazuchi, JS Shimokita, HMAS Toowoomba. Line from Subic Bay staging area to West Philippine Sea exercise zone. Chinese vessels shadowed at distance. Source: Manila Bulletin (April 30).

label: China Patrol/Research Vessels: Fiery Cross → Sandy Cay 1 — May 3, 2026
notes: Four Chinese vessels were identified at Sandy Cay 1 in the Spratly Islands on May 3, 2026, conducting what the Philippines called 'illegal research.' Incident coincided with Atin Ito civilian coalition planting the Philippine flag at dawn. China accused Philippines of 'illegal landing' of 5 nationals; Philippines threatened to deploy aircraft and ships to expel the Chinese vessels. Route assessed from Fiery Cross Reef command hub to Sandy Cay 1 near Pag-asa/Thitu Island. Sources: Malay Mail, Free Malaysia Today, OneNews.PH.

label: Balikatan 2026 CLLFX-N: Laoag Ilocos Norte → Luzon Strait Approach — May 4, 2026
notes: Counter-Landing Live Fire Exercise North (CLLFX-N) at La Paz Sand Dunes, Laoag, Ilocos Norte on May 4, 2026 (Balikatan Day 15). Philippine, US, and Japanese forces used HIMARS, Apache Longbow helicopters, and 105mm howitzers to simulate defense of Northern Luzon coastline. Line shows the Northern Luzon coastal approach corridor toward the Luzon Strait defended by the exercise. Companion to the CLLFX-South at Palawan (Day 8, April 27). Sources: PNA, Manila Bulletin, Manila Times, GMA News.

label: CCG 3103 Shadows Atin Ito Civilian Mission — May 2, 2026
notes: China Coast Guard vessel CCG 3103 shadowed the Atin Ito civilian coalition's 4th West Philippine Sea mission on May 2, 2026 — the night before the group's successful flag-planting at Sandy Cay 1. Philippine Coast Guard issued radio challenges asserting China has no jurisdiction in Philippine EEZ. Despite surveillance, Atin Ito landed on Sandy Cay 1 at dawn on May 3. Source: Manila Times (May 2, 2026).

label: China Research Vessel Xiang Yang Hong 33 — Reed Bank Survey, May 8, 2026
notes: China's research vessel Xiang Yang Hong 33 conducted a 'marine ecological survey' near Iroquois Reef at the southern end of Reed Bank (Recto Bank) on May 8, 2026 — opening a new Philippine EEZ flashpoint. China accused Philippine Coast Guard Islander aircraft of 'deliberately approaching and harassing' the vessel. Both sides issued warnings of potential countermeasures. Reed Bank is ~85 nm from Palawan, firmly within the Philippine EEZ under UNCLOS. China requires Philippine government consent for marine scientific research in Philippine EEZ waters, which the Philippines denies it provided. Line from CCG South Sea Base area to Reed Bank survey location.

label: Balikatan 2026 SINKEX: Japan-US-AU-PH Anti-Ship Missiles → Target Vessel Off Ilocos Norte — May 6, 2026
notes: Ship Sinking Exercise (SINKEX) by Japan, US, Australia, and Philippine forces off Ilocos Norte coast on May 6, 2026 (Balikatan Day 17). Japan fired anti-ship missiles against a decommissioned vessel — Japan's first combat troop deployment to the Philippines since WWII. Line shows missile trajectory from Ilocos Norte coast to target area in South China Sea. Builds trilateral sea-denial capability at Luzon Strait approach. Source: Bloomberg (May 6, 2026).

label: CCG Chuanshan Rights-Safeguarding Training: CCG Base → Scarborough Shoal — May 9, 2026
notes: China Coast Guard vessel Chuanshan conducted 'comprehensive maritime rights safeguarding and law enforcement training' at Scarborough Shoal on May 9, 2026 — the day after the 48th ASEAN Leaders' Summit closed in Cebu without a binding South China Sea Code of Conduct. China.org.cn (official state media) announced the exercise. Assessed as deliberate post-summit counter-signaling, consistent with China's pattern of CCG operations at Scarborough during major diplomatic events. The Chuanshan deployment follows the April 2026 floating barrier installation at Scarborough's lagoon entrance and the April 30 PLA STC combat readiness patrols at the same location during Balikatan 2026. Three concurrent SCS flashpoints: Reed Bank (Xiang Yang Hong 33 May 8), Second Thomas Shoal (ongoing), Scarborough Shoal (Chuanshan). Source: China.org.cn, May 9, 2026.

label: PLA AGI-797 ELINT Ship: Yulin Naval Base → WPS Monitoring Position — Balikatan 2026
notes: China's PLA Navy Type 815A Auxiliary General Intelligence ship AGI-797 operated in the West Philippine Sea during Balikatan 2026 (April 20 – May 8, 2026), positioned in international waters to collect signals intelligence (SIGINT) on the allied exercise force of 17,000 troops from 7 nations. The Type 815A is China's most capable ELINT platform, equipped with wideband signal interception systems, radar emission analysis, and communications intercept arrays. Deployment confirmed in post-exercise analysis (May 12-14). Line from Yulin Naval Base (Hainan) to approximate monitoring position in the West Philippine Sea north of the Spratly Islands.

label: PLA 8 Warships + 9 CCG: Post-Balikatan Mass Presence at Scarborough Shoal — May 4-11, 2026
notes: AFP WPS monitoring report (released May 13, 2026) documents 8 PLAN warships and 9 CCG cutters concentrated at Scarborough Shoal during May 4-11 — the largest combined PLA-CCG presence at Scarborough in official AFP records. Total WPS deployment: 35 Chinese vessels (15 PLAN + 20 CCG) at 4 locations: Scarborough (8+9), Pag-asa (3+3), Escoda Shoal (3+2), Ayungin/Second Thomas (1+6). No aggressive actions reported during Balikatan 2026. Assessed as China's post-exercise shadow-exercise monitoring and deterrence posture. Deployed simultaneously with ongoing marine nature reserve dispute (unanswered DFA protest May 11) and Reed Bank standoff (Day 7). Line from Zhanjiang South Sea Fleet HQ to Scarborough Shoal.

label: Xiang Yang Hong 33 Shifts: Reed Bank → Pag-asa Territorial Sea — May 16-18, 2026
notes: China's research vessel Xiang Yang Hong 33, which had been surveying near Iroquois Reef at Reed Bank since May 7, moved into the 12-nautical-mile territorial sea of Pag-asa (Thitu) Island, escorted by CCG vessels 5101 and 5309. Chinese personnel were ferried via RHIBs and rubber boats onto Sandy Cay 2 and Sandy Cay 3, both within Pag-asa's territorial sea. PCG Islander aircraft 4177 challenged the vessels. PCG launched a formal investigation on May 18; China's Global Times characterized Philippine aircraft operations as 'harassment.' This represents an escalation from EEZ violation (UNCLOS Art. 246) to direct territorial sea incursion and physical landing on Philippine sandbars. Line from Reed Bank survey position to Pag-asa Island. Sources: Philippine Star, PNA, Manila Bulletin Tempo (May 18, 2026).

label: CCG 4305 Unauthorized Patrol: 48nm Off Zambales — May 19, 2026
notes: China Coast Guard vessel CCG 4305 was flagged by Canada's Dark Vessel Detection Program approximately 48–50.1 nautical miles west of Pandaquit, Zambales — inside the Philippine EEZ off Luzon's west coast. PCG Piper Navajo aircraft 302 (from La Union Airport) visually confirmed at 8:40 a.m. BRP Cape San Agustin dispatched by PCG Commandant Admiral Gavan. Chinese vessel made no response to multiple radio challenges. PCG pledged to 'never allow normalization of illegal patrols' off Zambales. Second simultaneous Chinese intrusion on May 19 alongside Xiang Yang Hong 33 operations near Pag-asa Island — demonstrating a multi-vector pressure campaign extending to Luzon's western coast. Line from Scarborough Shoal (assessed staging/patrol area) to CCG 4305 position off Zambales. Sources: Philippine Star, Manila Bulletin, GMA News, Newsweek, PNA (May 19, 2026).

label: China CCG-Militia Dual-Ring Perimeter: Zhanjiang → Scarborough Shoal — May 31, 2026
notes: China established a 16+ vessel dual-ring perimeter at Scarborough Shoal on May 31, 2026: 9 CCG vessels (outer ring, 20-40nm from shoal) + 7 maritime militia (inner cordon, 5-17nm). Philippines warned of threat. Concurrent with USCG Midgett + PCG BRP Melchora Aquino joint presence ops. Most comprehensive Chinese force posture at Scarborough since 2012 seizure. Sources: Manila Times, AP/WHBL, Jakarta Post, May 31, 2026.

label: USCG Midgett + PCG BRP Melchora Aquino: Subic Bay → Scarborough Shoal Joint Ops, May 28-31, 2026
notes: US Coast Guard cutter Midgett (WMSL-757, 4,500 tons, National Security Cutter) and Philippine Coast Guard cutter BRP Melchora Aquino conducted 5-day joint maritime presence operations near Scarborough Shoal (May 28-31, 2026). Direct counter-presence to China's concurrent 16+ vessel CCG-militia perimeter formation at Scarborough. Most direct US-Philippine coast guard bilateral presence at Scarborough since 2023 MDT coast guard extension. Sources: Manila Times, AP/WHBL, May 31, 2026.

label: China CCG Patrol East of Taiwan — June 8, 2026 (2nd Iteration)
notes: China dispatched Chinese Coast Guard and other PRC government vessels to patrol waters east of Taiwan for a second time (first iteration June 1) — a direct operational response to the Philippines-Japan announcement (May 28, Tokyo, Marcos-Takaichi summit) of formal talks to delimit their EEZ/continental shelf boundary. Chinese FM spokeswoman Mao Ning declared May 29 that the talks are 'entirely illegal and invalid' and that Beijing holds exclusive EEZ/continental shelf rights in the waters east of Taiwan. Chinese state media (Global Times, CGTN) framed the patrols as 'responsive law enforcement operations' demonstrating China's 'capability and resolve.' Sources: Global Times, Hong Kong Free Press (May 29, 2026); GlobalSecurity.org/Global Times (June 7, 2026).

label: 4th PH-US Bilateral Maritime Cooperative Activity — Scarborough Shoal, June 14-19, 2026
notes: The Philippines and United States conducted their fourth Bilateral Maritime Cooperative Activity (MCA) of 2026, a 6-day joint patrol (June 14-19) near Bajo de Masinloc (Scarborough Shoal). Philippine assets: frigate BRP Diego Silang (FFG-07), FA-50 fighter jets, AW109 helicopter, C-208B aircraft, PCG cutters BRP Melchora Aquino and BRP Sindangan. US assets: USCGC Charles Moulthrope (WPC-1141), USCGC Emlen Tunnell (WPC-1145), P-8A Poseidon patrol aircraft, 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment personnel. Chinese forces shadowing the activity included two Jiangkai-class frigates, one Jiangdao-class corvette, an auxiliary tanker, and maritime patrol aircraft. Final-day surveillance (June 17) confirmed a Chinese floating research platform inside the shoal's lagoon had been removed. Source: Manila Bulletin, June 20, 2026.

label: BRP Diego Silang vs. 4 PLA Warships — Scarborough Shoal Standoff, June 21, 2026
notes: Philippine Navy frigate BRP Diego Silang (Miguel Malvar-class, FFG-07), fresh off the 4th PH-US Bilateral Maritime Cooperative Activity, encountered a single Chinese naval vessel and then four PLA warships in a rare, direct naval stand-off approximately 124 nautical miles off the Philippine coast near Scarborough Shoal on Saturday, June 21, 2026 — the same day Manila concluded Exercise Salaknib 2026. Chinese and Philippine naval personnel exchanged radio challenges ordering each other to leave the area; despite being outnumbered, the Philippine frigate continued its patrol and launched its onboard AW109 helicopter while underway at 18 knots. China accused the helicopter of an unauthorized 'airspace' incursion. No casualties or damage reported; Beijing issued no public statement. Source: South China Morning Post (published June 23, 2026, citing GMA Network's 24 Oras Weekend).

label: CCG Personnel Strike PH Navy Sailor With Baton — Jul 20, 2026
notes: China Coast Guard personnel rammed a Philippine Navy RHIB and struck a sailor on the head with a wooden baton near Second Thomas (Ayungin) Shoal, causing a head injury. First of three China-Philippines clashes during the week of July 20-24, 2026.

label: CCG Water Cannon Blocks Fisher Resupply — Jul 23, 2026
notes: China Coast Guard fired a water cannon for over two minutes and conducted a dangerous maneuver to block a Philippine mission resupplying fuel and food to Filipino fishers at Scarborough Shoal. 12 CCG vessels and 3 maritime militia vessels involved. Second of three clashes during the week of July 20-24, 2026.

label: CCG Water Cannon on PH Vessel Carrying CNN Crew — Jul 24, 2026
notes: China Coast Guard fired a water cannon at a Philippine vessel carrying a CNN news crew near Scarborough Shoal — the third China-Philippines clash in a single week. Manila called it part of a pattern of 'repeated aggressive, unprofessional and illegal' Chinese actions.

label: Japan-Philippines-US Multilateral Maritime Cooperative Activity — Jul 21-25, 2026
notes: Japan, the Philippines and the US conducted a joint Multilateral Maritime Cooperative Activity (MMCA) in the South China Sea, deploying naval vessels and aircraft, days after the July 20 baton incident at Second Thomas Shoal. China criticized the drills as provocative.

label: PLA Southern Theater Command Drills Near Scarborough Shoal (Disputed) — Aug 1, 2026
notes: China's PLA Southern Theater Command announced joint naval-air combat-readiness drills near Scarborough Shoal involving bombers, frigates, helicopters and coast guard vessels, days after the Philippines' UN extended continental shelf claim. The Philippines' National Maritime Council disputed the claim on Aug 3 as 'not credible,' saying only vessel presence — not live drills — was detected.

label: China Surges Amphibious Group + H-6K Bombers to Scarborough Shoal — Aug 1-3, 2026
notes: China deployed a Type 052D destroyer, Type 071 LPD (with embarked landing craft and Z-20 helicopter), Type 054A frigate and Type 056A corvette, plus at least two H-6K bombers armed with YJ-12 anti-ship cruise missiles, to Scarborough Shoal — 120nm off the Philippines. PLA Southern Theater Command said the drills 'safeguard China's territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests.'
platform: Type 052D DDG, Type 071 LPD, Type 054A FFG, Type 056A corvette, H-6K bomber (YJ-12)

label: PLA Southern Theater Command Routine Patrol — Response to PH 'Joint Patrols,' Aug 21-25, 2026
notes: PLA Southern Theater Command spokesperson Senior Captain Zhai Shichen said naval and air forces conducted a routine patrol across the South China Sea from Aug 21-25, 2026, framed as a response to the Philippines 'co-opting countries outside the region to conduct so-called joint patrols.' No specific patrol coordinates were disclosed; anchor point shown is Scarborough Shoal, the theater's most active flashpoint this period.

label: RORE Mission to BRP Sierra Madre — Aug 22, 2026
notes: PCG vessels BRP Malabrigo and BRP Teresa Magbanua ran a resupply mission to BRP Sierra Madre at Ayungin (Second Thomas) Shoal, shadowed throughout by China Coast Guard and maritime militia vessels under the Marcos-confirmed 'provisional understanding' with Beijing.

label: 19th MMCA (PH-US-Australia) — Sabina Shoal Radio Challenge, Aug 21-25, 2026
notes: BRP Diego Silang, USS Santa Barbara and HMAS Supply conducted the 19th Multilateral Maritime Cooperative Activity while shadowed by a Chinese destroyer, frigate, missile boat and corvette; Chinese warship 536 radioed the Philippine frigate near Sabina Shoal asserting sovereignty and ordering it to leave, which Manila rejected citing UNCLOS and its EEZ.
platform: BRP Diego Silang, BRP Teresa Magbanua, USS Santa Barbara, HMAS Supply
